title: Stack Frames [Local Variables]
description:
## Stack Frames
So far you've used registers for everything. But what if you need more variables than registers? Use the stack.

### The prologue:
```asm
my_func:
    push rbp          ; save old base pointer
    mov rbp, rsp      ; set new base pointer
    sub rsp, 16       ; allocate 16 bytes for local vars
```

### Accessing local variables:
```asm
    mov dword [rbp - 4], 42    ; local var 1
    mov dword [rbp - 8], 100   ; local var 2
```

### The epilogue:
```asm
    mov rsp, rbp      ; deallocate locals
    pop rbp           ; restore old base pointer
    ret
```

This is exactly what C compilers generate. Every function call creates a stack frame:
```
|  return address  |  <- pushed by call
|  old rbp         |  <- pushed by prologue
|  local var 1     |  [rbp - 4]
|  local var 2     |  [rbp - 8]
|  ...             |  <- rsp points here
```

**Step through with the debugger and watch rbp and rsp change!**

---
## Assignment:
Write a function `swap_add` that takes two numbers in `rdi` and `rsi`, stores them in local stack variables, swaps them, then returns their sum. Use a proper stack frame with prologue/epilogue.
setupCode:
section .data
    pass_msg db "PASS", 10
    pass_len equ $ - pass_msg
    fail_msg db "FAIL", 10
    fail_len equ $ - fail_msg

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
swap_add:
    ; prologue
    ; store rdi and rsi in local vars
    ; swap them
    ; add and return in rax
    ; epilogue
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    mov rdi, 5
    mov rsi, 3
    call swap_add
    cmp rax, 8
    jne .fail
    mov rdi, 10
    mov rsi, 20
    call swap_add
    cmp rax, 30
    jne .fail
    mov rdi, 0
    mov rsi, 0
    call swap_add
    cmp rax, 0
    jne .fail
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, pass_msg
    mov rdx, pass_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.fail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, fail_msg
    mov rdx, fail_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Prologue: push rbp, mov rbp rsp, sub rsp 16. Store rdi at [rbp-4] and rsi at [rbp-8]. Swap by loading into registers and storing back. Add both and put in rax. Epilogue: mov rsp rbp, pop rbp, ret.
